newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine revises '96 beet forecast down to 24 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine revises '96 beet forecast down to 24 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine has revised down the forecast for its 1996 sugar beet crop to 24 million tonnes from 26 million tonnes, with both figures below 1995 output of 30 million tonnes, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Friday.
"The Ukrainian sugar beet harvesting campaign is nearly over," Valentyn Tymoshenko, deputy head of the crop department, told Reuters.
"Unfortunately, drought this year spoiled our hopes for a good harvest and we have changed our forecast," he added.
He said the beet harvest was nearly finished and stood at 23.68 million tonnes, adding, "There could be a small contribution from the private sector."
In all, 1.189 million hectares, or 98 percent of the total area sown to sugar beets, have been harvested. Ukraine harvested 1.380 million hectares last year.
Kiev's forecast at the beginning of the summer for the 1996 beet harvest was 27 million tonnes.

Specialists have blamed the poor outlook this year on drought at the beginning of the growing season, although the largely state-owned agriculture sector suffers from shortages of fuel, equipment, pesticides and herbicides.
Average yields stood at 19.9 tonnes, compared to 22.2 tonnes in 1995.
Ukraine on Thursday revised down its refined sugar output forecast to 2.6 million tonnes from 3.485 million tonnes last year.
